note: Rewritten from Roonwal & Chhotani (1997), entry 91; the original is in English. The original describes only the soldier and worker, the alate being recorded as unknown. The antennae and some legs of the specimens examined were damaged, and the original gives neither the number of antennal segments nor the hind tibial spurs, so these are truthfully left unrecorded here. The diagnostic characters follow the soldier key in that work (p. 572). The synonymy list, literature citations, figure numbers, type-specimen records and distribution records have been removed.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier larger (total length with mandibles 9.9–10.5 mm); head length to mandible base 3.10–3.30 mm, width 2.25–2.32 mm; head subrectangular with nearly parallel sides, the antennal fossae (the concavities at the antennal bases) not prominent and not deep, fontanelle nearly circular, mandibles relatively long for the head (mandible length/head length ratio 0.73–0.76). The similarly large congener faveolus has a rectangular–oval head with slightly convex sides converging anteriorly, prominent and deep antennal fossae, an oval fontanelle and shorter mandibles (ratio 0.60–0.67). Alate unknown.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head reddish brown, the rest of the body yellow. Head and body moderately hairy, the hairs short and stiff. Body length 9.9–10.5 mm. Head slightly elongate, subrectangular, slightly narrowed anteriorly; longer than wide (length to mandible base 3.10–3.30 mm, width 2.25–2.32 mm); frons sloping gently forwards. Fontanelle minute, circular, situated in the anterior 1/3 of the head; distance from occiput to fontanelle 2.18 mm. Labrum subquadrate (length 0.50–0.54 mm, width 0.55–0.67 mm), rounded apically, only slightly wider than long, with several hairs on the apical half. Anteclypeus narrow; boundary between postclypeus and frons indistinct. Mandibles long (2.35–2.40 mm) and stout, slightly shorter than the head; narrowing towards the apex, the tips acute and slightly incurved; inner margin with a small tooth at about the basal 1/3 and another, stouter tooth near the base. Eyes reduced, represented by small dark spots; ocelli absent. Antennae incomplete; segment 2 smaller than segment 3. Postmentum long, club-shaped, with a slender waist; median length 2.37–2.50 mm, maximum width 0.80–0.87 mm, waist width 0.30–0.35 mm; apex club-shaped with an anterior and a posterior lobe, the posterior only slightly wider than the anterior. Pronotum flat, trapezoidal, narrower than the head; width 1.92 mm, length 1.25–1.30 mm; median concavity on both anterior and posterior margins. Fore femur stout, with 3 apical tibial spurs; the other legs damaged. Cerci short, 2-segmented; abdominal spines absent.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Pale yellow, moderately hairy, the hairs short and stiff. Body length 5.5–6.5 mm. Head circular, length 1.5–1.6 mm, width 1.67–1.80 mm, slightly narrowed posteriorly. Fontanelle small, situated in the middle of the head. Labrum dome-shaped, narrower at the base, with several hairs on the apical half. Eyes small; ocelli absent. Mandibles of the Stylotermes type. Antennae incomplete. Pronotum flat, narrower than the head; length 0.62–0.75 mm, width 1.27–1.42 mm; anterior margin with a broad median concavity, posterior margin with a small median concavity. Femora stout; apical tibial spur formula 3:2:2. Cerci short, 2-segmented; abdominal spines absent.
